issues.body: The new comment says HASH-BEFORE-MEMCMP is already present on EVERY DEDUP PATH and treats the requested stored 64-bit comparison as complete. But self.table is described as relying on hashbrown's 7-bit h2 tag, which can invoke the equality/string comparison for entries whose remaining 57 hash bits differ. That is not the requested full 64-bit prefilter. The new mapped_find_compares_full_hash_before_eq test exercises only the mmap path and therefore cannot support the every-path claim. As written, the change either leaves the stated requirement incomplete or materially overstates what was verified.
issues.fix_hint: Either implement and test a full-hash-before-equality prefilter for the in-memory/sharded/spill paths that require it, or narrow the documentation and PR scope to state precisely that only mapped_find has a full 64-bit gate and that the in-memory path intentionally retains the h2-only prefilter. If the requirement permits that tradeoff, add a test appropriate to the actual claimed invariant rather than describing the mmap-only test as pinning every dedup path.
issues.title: Full-hash prefilter is not verified on every deduplication path

verdict.summary: The whole-chunk UTF-8 validation makes the new unchecked conversion sound on the shown parser paths, and the boundary-focused tests are substantive. However, the dictionary portion claims that the requested full-hash-before-string-compare invariant is already present on every deduplication path, while its own explanation shows that the ordinary in-memory HashTable path checks only hashbrown's 7-bit h2 tag before invoking equality. The added test covers only mapped_find, so it cannot substantiate the PR's broader claim or completion of that requirement.
